title: A/B Test Sequential Stopping Rules for Safe Online Preference Tuning

original_idea.body:
# Sequential Stopping Rules for Safe Online Preference Tuning

**Problem:** Practitioners lack principled stopping rules to halt training when safety degrades.

**Direction:** Use SPRT/always-valid inference to continuously test safety on a probe set and auto-stop at boundary crossing.

**Why it matters:** A peeking-safe auto-stop for alignment training.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2507.03662; arXiv:2510.02712.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: An auto-stop guardrail is useful but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SPRT/e-value stopping on a probe metric across a fine-tune chain; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused auto-stop demonstration; needs a drifting fine-tune chain.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, small probe set; independent-friendly monitoring tool.

low_compute.reasoning: A chain of small fine-tune increments plus inference; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Sequential testing is standard; its application to safe alignment-stopping may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sequential testing standard; alignment-stopping application may be open.
